litigation_timing.support: The amendment made a minister answerable to the Prime Minister for his functions (s. 4). It also added s. 21א: the PM may, after notifying the Government, remove a minister from office, effective 48 hours after the letter is delivered, and must inform the Knesset. No petition or appeal about the PM's power to remove a minister was found pending before the Supreme Court on 19 May 1981. IDI says only that the law was silent on dismissal before 1981 (except dismissal for voting against the Government) and cites no litigation earlier than HCJ 5261/04. The Abuhatzira affair was under way at the time (immunity lifted 13 Jan 1981), but no Supreme Court proceeding seeking his removal was found.
litigation_timing.note: No judgment identified to which the enactment responded.

litigation_timing.support: The Government tabled the bill in June 1978 and it passed on 28 Feb 1984, about six years later. According to the explanatory notes as reported, it gathers the principles of the Courts Law 1957 and the Judges Law 1953 into a framework Basic Law and leaves the detail to those statutes. No petition or appeal was found pending at passage that concerned a rule the Basic Law changed. In this pass the Basic Law's own text was not compared clause by clause with the 1957 and 1953 statutes.
litigation_timing.note: No judgment identified to which the enactment responded.

litigation_timing.support: Amendment 10 numbered s. 6 as (א) and added s. 6(ב). Under 6(ב), an Israeli citizen who also holds a foreign citizenship that the other state's law allows him to give up may not be a Knesset candidate until he has done everything required on his side to give it up, to the satisfaction of the chair of the Central Elections Committee (s. 6(ב) was repealed in 1996 by Amendment 22). No Supreme Court petition or election appeal on dual-citizen candidacy was found pending on 19 May 1987. No election was in progress, and the rule applied only from the 12th Knesset elections.

No petition about the security cabinet's composition or an advisory staff was found pending on 5 Feb 1991.

litigation_timing.support: Amendment 13 numbered s. 21 as (א) and added s. 21(ב). The Rules of Procedure may empower committees to summon office-holders in the civil service, local authorities, religious councils, statutory corporations and government companies, and to require information from them, subject to legal, professional and fiduciary limits and with a witness's rights. The summons goes through the minister concerned 'ובתיאום עמו' (changed in 2000 to 'או בידיעתו'), and the minister or head of body may appear instead. No petition about committees' power to compel officials was found pending on 23 Jul 1991. The IDI piece gives no litigation history for the provision.

litigation_timing.support: Amendment 8 added the same words to s. 5(ב1) (defector may not be a minister) and s. 34(ב) (defector may not be a deputy minister): '; הוראה זו לא תחול על התפלגות סיעה בתנאים שנקבעו בחוק הבחירות לכנסת; לענין סעיף קטן זה, "פרישה מסיעה" – כמשמעותה בסעיף 6א לחוק-יסוד: הכנסת'. A faction split that meets the statutory conditions is thereby taken out of the bar. Context: Yiud split from Tzomet on 7 Feb 1994 and joined the Rabin government in January 1995 (Segev as minister, Goldfarb as deputy minister). No Supreme Court petition or appeal about the Yiud split, its recognition, or the defection bar was found pending on 19 Dec 1994.

litigation_timing.support: Amendment 4 replaced s. 9, the right to nominate a candidate for Prime Minister. Previously a faction or factions of the outgoing Knesset with at least 10 members could nominate, or 50,000 voters. Now nominations come from parties: a party (or parties) that submitted a Knesset list and is represented by faction(s) with at least 10 members, or a party that submitted a list and has written support from 50,000 voters. In special elections, parties represented by faction(s) with at least 10 members. No petition about the right to nominate a PM candidate was found pending on 28 Feb 1996.
litigation_timing.note: No judgment identified to which the enactment responded.

deviations: Every 'No' rests on finding no evidence in web searches and secondary sources, not on a docket search. The judiciary's database (supremedecisions.court.gov.il) was not searched by party or subject; only one judgment PDF (HCJ 3132/15) was downloaded by direct link. Nevo was not used (www.nevo.co.il returned HTTP 403 to curl on 2026-10-22). Versa, ACRI, Adalah and the Movement for Quality Government sites were not searched. A reviewer should check dockets for the period before each passage date, especially seq 39 (Yiud split; the Segev and Goldfarb appointments; Tzomet, December 1994), seq 42 (the PM holding vacated portfolios, 1993–95) and seqs 45 and 48 (party-only lists and PM nominations, February 1996).

fs.knesset.gov.il (enacted-law PDFs and bills) redirected to https://www.knesset.gov.il/maintenance-page-geo for both curl and WebFetch on 2026-10-22. So none of the bills' explanatory notes were read: ה"ח 1537, 1748, 2030, 2061, 2017, 2323, 2362, 2499, 2514, 2497, and the 1978 Judiciary bill. Those notes are the most likely place for a stated litigation background. Enactment texts were taken from the archived Nevo consolidations named in the sheet (version history read from the markup) and from he.wikisource raw wikitext. For seq 19 they were also taken from a search engine's summary of the scanned PDF. For seq 22 the Basic Law text itself was not read.
web.archive.org refused connections intermittently and WebFetch cannot fetch it; the snapshots were fetched with curl to stdout after retries.

HCJ 5364/94 Velner v. Chairman of the Israeli Labor Party, PD 49(1) 758, was filed in 1994 and concerns a political agreement (Bendor and Cohen, משפט וממשל ג 297 (1995)). Four searches did not establish which agreement it concerned. If it concerned the Labor–Yiud deal, it could bear on seq 39 and should be checked.

Frame points for the reviewer. Seq 45 (Knesset Amendment 19) was repealed two days later by s. 4 of Amendment 21, which re-enacted s. 5א in nearly the same words. Seq 48 (1992 Government law Amendment 4) repealed Amendment 3, published 27.2.1996 from the same bill as seq 45 (ה"ח 2499). Seq 42's s. 2 is also Amendment No. 2 to the 1992 law, which matches the sheet's 'amends both'. Wikisource lists Government Amendment No. 8 (תשנ"ה, 42) under both the 1968 and the 1992 law, but Nevo's 1992-law footnotes do not list it; the sheet says 1968 only.

Seq 28 is not the February 1991 anti-defection amendment. That amendment is Government Amendment No. 6, enacted inside Basic Law: The Knesset (Amendment No. 12). Seq 28 (Amendment No. 5) created the national-security ministerial committee and advisory staff.
